openai.label: OpenAI

amazon-bedrock.label: Amazon Bedrock
unverified: The ids are the us. inference profiles; a login whose AWS_REGION is outside the US needs the matching eu., au., jp. or global. prefix.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
The prices are Bedrock's US regional ones (10% above its global endpoint), matching the us. ids.

bedrock-mantle.label: Bedrock Mantle
unverified: AWS lists the 5.5 models on Mantle in very few regions (Opus 5.5 in us-east-1); a region without one answers that the model is not found.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
AWS does not say whether Mantle bills at Bedrock's global or regional (10% higher) rate; the global one is used.

google-vertex.label: Google Vertex AI
unverified: Haiku 5.5 is served in the US and EU multi-regions and global; a single region may not have it.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
The prices are Vertex AI's global-endpoint ones; a regional or multi-region endpoint costs 10% more.

microsoft-foundry.label: Microsoft Foundry
unverified: Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
Foundry bills Anthropic's standard rates, which are the prices here; a transcript names your deployment rather than these aliases, so a session is priced only when the two match.

zai.label: GLM / Z.ai
unverified: Z.ai's Claude Code page shows two mappings; this one (GLM-5.3 for opus and sonnet, GLM-5.3-Flash for haiku) is its manual setup.
Z.ai lists no cache-write price (cached storage is free for now); a written token is charged as input.

kimi.label: Kimi / Moonshot
unverified: Kimi's guide says kimi-k2.7-code always thinks, while its model table says it does not; Ferretry offers no effort choice for it.
Kimi charges one cache-write price per request in analytics: K3's 5-minute one ($3); its 1-hour write costs $6.
Kimi lists no cache-write price for the K2.7 Code models; a written token is charged as input.

minimax.label: MiniMax
unverified: MiniMax maps every Claude Code slot to MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview; MiniMax-M3's reasoning controls are not documented on that page.
MiniMax lists no cache-write price; a written token is charged as input.
MiniMax-M3 costs twice as much over 512K input tokens; the price is the lower one.
MiniMax's pricing page lists MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, without -Preview; its price is used for the preview id.
MiniMax-M2.7 is not on MiniMax's pricing page, so it has no price.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
unverified: DeepSeek charges half price off-peak; the prices are its peak (full) ones.
DeepSeek lists no cache-write price; a written token is a cache miss, charged as input.

qwen.label: Qwen / Model Studio
unverified: Per-model context windows and reasoning controls are not on Alibaba's Claude Code page.
Qwen prices rise with a request's input length; the prices are the lowest tier.
Cache reads (10% of input) and cache writes (125% of input) are Model Studio's general rule, not per-model prices.
qwen3.7-plus shows a limited-time discount; whether its price is the discounted one is not stated.

openrouter.label: OpenRouter
unverified: OpenRouter's Codex guide names only ~openai/gpt-sol-latest; whether Astra and Luna have ~latest aliases is not documented.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
The prices are those of the models the ~latest aliases resolve to today (Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol); OpenRouter may move an alias.
A transcript may name the resolved model (anthropic/claude-opus-5.5) rather than the alias, and that spelling is not priced.

vercel-ai-gateway.label: Vercel AI Gateway
unverified: Vercel's guide shows claude-code/anthropic/claude-opus-5; the 5.5 ids here follow its documented format and were not read on that page.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
Vercel lists no 1-hour cache write price; Anthropic's, which every other Vercel price matches, is used.

gateway.label: Your gateway
unverified: A gateway serves whatever names its owner configured; these are Anthropic's ids, which a gateway may rename.
Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much for a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so its price is the lower one and a long-prompt session is under-counted.
A gateway charges whatever its owner arranged; the prices are Anthropic's list prices for these ids.

azure-openai.label: Azure OpenAI
unverified: Which GPT-6 models a given Azure region offers is not on Microsoft's Codex page.
GPT-6 models cost more for a request over 272K input tokens; analytics prices whole sessions, so the price is the short-context one and a long-context session is under-counted.
The prices are Azure's global deployment ones; a Data Zone deployment costs 10-20% more.

ollama.label: Ollama (local)
unverified: gpt-oss:20b and gpt-oss:120b run on this machine through Ollama; there is no per-token price, so they have none.

presets.label: Anthropic API key
presets.summary: Claude Code with an API key from the Claude Platform console, billed per token.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.description: the API key, sent as x-api-key
the API key, sent as x-api-key

test.note: Lists the models the key can use. Spends nothing.

quota.note: An API key has no usage endpoint of its own, so cost is counted from the transcript at Anthropic's prices.

presets.label: Amazon Bedrock (AWS profile)
presets.summary: Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock, using an AWS profile from ~/.aws on this machine. The profile is named, never copied.
unverified: No free read proves Bedrock invoke rights; ListInferenceProfiles proves the profile signs in, not that it may run a model.

AWS_REGION.description: the region Bedrock is called in
the region Bedrock is called in

test.reason: Bedrock needs AWS request signing, which Ferretry does not do. Check the profile with `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile <name>`.

quota.note: AWS Service Quotas reports limits, not what is used, so cost is counted from the transcript at Bedrock's prices.

presets.label: Amazon Bedrock (API key)
presets.summary: Claude Code through Amazon Bedrock with a Bedrock API key, which skips the AWS credential chain.
unverified: No free read is documented for a Bedrock API key; CountTokens does not support every Claude model.

AWS_REGION.description: the region Bedrock is called in
the region Bedrock is called in

test.reason: Bedrock documents no free read for an API key, so Ferretry does not spend one to test it. Start an agent on it to check.

quota.note: AWS Service Quotas reports limits, not what is used, so cost is counted from the transcript at Bedrock's prices.

presets.label: Bedrock Mantle (AWS profile)
